MINUTES
  MALIBU PLANNING COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  OCTOBER 16, 2023
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS AND TELECONFERENCED
  6:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held in a hybrid format that allowed members of the public to
participate in-person and remotely via Zoom.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Peak called the meeting to order at 6:32 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Skylar Peak, Vice Chair John G. Mazza, Commissioners Dennis R.
  Smith, Jeffrey D. Jennings, Kraig Hill

  ABSENT:

  ALSO PRESENT: Pat Donegan, Assistant City Attorney; Adrian Fernandez, Assistant
  Planning Director; Parker Davis, Media Technician; Gail Duncan, Office Assistant; and
  Rebecca Evans, Recording Secretary

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Councilmember Stewart led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Vice Chair Mazza moved and Chair Peak seconded a motion to approve the agenda
  as recommended by staff, continuing Item No. 5.C. to the November 6, 2023
  Regular Planning Commission meeting and asked to dedicate the meeting to Walt
  Keller.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recording Secretary Evans reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on October 6,2023; the amended agenda was properly posted on October 10, 2023.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of October 16, 2023
  Page 2 of 8

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS
  None.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Councilmember Stewart thanked Commissioner Jennings for his extensive service
  to the City and to the Planning Commission. Commissioner Jennings was an
  advocate for residents since prior to cityhood. He served on several City Councils,
  as a mayor, Chair of the Planning Commission and was always a statesman and
  diplomat who was looked up to and admired. When Councilmember Stewart was
  elected, there was no question who he wanted to serve as his appointee to the
  Planning Commission. Although Commissioner Jennings had planned to retire, he
  agreed to extend his service through October 2023 due to upcoming complex and
  high priority projects such as the Malibu Middle and High School Campus and the
  Accessory Dwelling Unit ordinance. Councilmember Stewart noted that
  Commissioner Jennings would never be able to be replaced and expressed the hope
  that all who followed him would try to emulate his wisdom, insight and diplomacy.
  He expressed thanks on behalf of himself and the residents of Malibu.

  Ann Doneen used her time to play the first three minutes of avideo with segments
  regarding a previously approved coastal development permit.

  Jo Drummond stated that the deck project at her home should not require any
  studies or permits when a larger project was approved in a landslide area without a
  variance requirement and only required an erosion study. She stated accessory
  structures in Big Rock had never been required to provide a variance for factor of
  safety and her specific property had never been subject to a landslide.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / STAFF COMMENTS

  Commissioner Smith wished Carolyn a happy birthday and told Commissioner
  Jennings it had been an honor to sit next to him as a member of the Planning
  Commission. Commissioner Jennings had always been gracious and generous with
  his time to discuss Commission items. He wished Commissioner Jennings and his
  wife Kris all the best.

  In response to Jo Drummond, Commissioner Hill agreed that her proposed deck did
  not appear to require the level of permitting requirements which had been asked
  for. He told her to contact the City Manager, City Council or the court if she had
  alleged unfair treatment or to request the City Council consider changes to the
  Code.

  Commissioner Hill stated the recent Poosh event was one example of how a special
  or temporary event can impact neighborhood parking and traffic safety. Pacaso
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of October 16, 2023
  Page 3 of 8

 houses recently been treated as timeshares in other coastal communities such as
 Newport Beach and Carmel and California Coastal Commission had allowed this.
 He asked staff whether this brought the City closer to adopting an ordinance.

Commissioner Hill stated Malibu was the most visitor serving city in California per
capita for daytime visitors. The Malibu Chamber of Commerce had recently
merged with the Palisades Chamber of Commerce. Regarding the Fair Political
Practices Commission (FPPC) complaint, City Attomey Rusin reported a City
Council closed session vote to send a response letter to the FPPC. Commissioner
Hill stated it was ironic that the conflict laws were about perception rather than
evidence of wrongdoing, yet Councilmembers named in the complaint voted on the
City’s response. He expressed the hope that legal experts in the field were being
brought in as consultants. Commissioner Hill thanked Commissioner Jennings for
his legal expertise, institutional memory and occasional laughs at his jokes. He
mentioned recent discussions regarding naming the Charmlee park visitors’ center
after Walt and Lucille Keller.

In response to Commissioner Hill, Assistant City Attorney Donegan cautioned that
the FPPC matter was not within the Planning Commission’s purview and the matter
was being diligently handled by the City Attorney’s office, including BBK experts
on FPPC concerns.

Vice Chair Mazza agreed with Commissioner Hill that an open session for City
Council discussion of the Ravel letter would have been preferable. He asked staff
to explain why Ms. Drummond’s deck could not be approved with an over-the-
counter permit. He noted that Walt Keller was the father of Malibu who fought
against two marinas, a nuclear power plant, a freeway, etc. over a long period of
time and worked to achieve cityhood and to preserve the unique nature of Malibu.

Commissioner Jennings thanked the group for their kind words. He learned early
on that local government could have an enormous impact on the residents of the
city. He stated the ability to be one of the five people who had a voice in making
these decisions had been a real privilege. Commissioner Jennings those who had
appointed him to serve and thanked the staff for making the job more pleasant than
it might otherwise have been.

Chair Peak noted that Commissioner Jennings was a very wise person and thanked
him for the positive impact he had made on many people’s lives. He asked if any
member of the Planning Commission had met with Jo Drummond to review the
situation with Planning staff and expressed a willingness to assist her if needed. He
stated that Walt Keller had a big impact through his public service and agreed with
the importance and impact of local government. Chair Peak stated it had been a
pleasure to serve with Commissioner Jennings and his experience would be missed.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of October 16, 2023
  Page 4 of 8

  In response to Chair Peak, Commissioner Jennings noted that members of the
  Planning Commission were not permitted to talk to staff regarding any specific
  projects based on Fair Political Practices Commission guidelines.

  Commissioner 1-lill stated that approvals should be simpler on the low end of
  projects.

  Chair Peak noted that although it might be tempting to compare Ms. Drummond’s
  project with a specific coastal development permit, the coastal development permit
  required far more reporting and scrutiny in advance of the hearing and a direct
  comparison was not appropriate.

  Assistant Planning Director Fernandez expressed thanks from the Planning
  Department staff for Commissioner Jennings service and wished him well in his
  future endeavors.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.

  B.  New Items

  I.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes of the October 2, 2023 Regular
  Planning Commission meeting.
  Staff Contact: Senior Administrative Analyst Evans, 456-2489, ext. 246

MOTION  Vice Chair Mazza moved and Commissioner Jennings seconded a motion
  to approve the minutes of the October 2, 2023 Regular Planning
  Commission meeting as amended to delete the word insanely, and
  incorporate two minor changes to Commissioner Hill’s comments under
  Item No. 2.B.

  The question was called and the motion unanimously.

ITEM 4  CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARINGS
  None.

ITEM 5  NEW PUBLIC HEARINGS

  A.  Zoning Text Amendment 23-003 Extend Deadlines for Nonconforming In-kind
  —

  Disaster Rebuild Projects
  Recommended Action: Adopt Planning Commission Resolution No. 23-45
  recommending the City Council adopt Zoning Text Amendment No. 23-003 to
  amend Malibu Municipal Code Section 17.60.020(C) to add three years to the
  deadline to initiate the planning application process and obtain building permits to
  rebuild a nonconforming structure that was damaged or destroyed in the Woolsey
  Fire and finding the action exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act.
  Staff Contact: Development and Operations Manager Salazar, 456-2489, ext. 245

  Assistant Planning Di rector Fernandez presented the staff report.

  Chair Peak opened the public comment portion of the hearing.

  Speakers: Peter Ireland; Josh Zavelia, Jaron Denson, Beatrice Zilinskas

  As there were no other speakers present, Chair Peak closed the public comment
  portion of the hearing and returned the matter to the table for discussion.

  The Commission directed questions to the applicant team and staff.

MOTION  Vice Chair Mazza moved and Chair Peak seconded a motion to adopt Planning
  Commission Resolution No. 23-45 recommending the City Council adopt Zoning
  Text Amendment No. 23-003 to amend Malibu Municipal Code Section
  17.60.020(C) to add three years to the deadline to initiate the planning application
  process and obtain building permits to rebuild a nonconforming structure that was
  damaged or destroyed in the Woolsey Fire and finding the action exempt from the
  California Environmental Quality Act.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.

RECESS  The meeting was recessed at 7:50 p.m. and resumed at 7:55 p.m. with all
  Commissioners on the dais.

  The Commission directed questions to the applicant team and staff.

MOTION  Vice Chair Mazza moved and Commissioner Hill seconded a motion to adopt
  Planning Commission Resolution No. 23-42, as amended, 1) adding a condition to,
  “Maintain a 5 ft walkway around the tank as required by the fire department and a
  10’ walking path in the public right-of-way (or within 7 ft of the fence) and
  maintained no higher than 15 feet.”; and 2) determining the project is exempt from
  the California Environmental Quality Act and approving Coastal Development
  Permit Amendment No. 20-017 to amend Coastal Development Permit No. 13-040
  for the installation of landscaping in the City’s public right-of-way to visually
  screen the recently approved water tank at 5723 Busch Drive

  The question was called and the motion failed 2-3, Commissioners Jennings, Smith
  and Peak dissenting.

SUBSTITUTE MOTION
  Chair Peak moved and Commissioner Jennings seconded a motion to adopt
  Planning Commission Resolution No. 23-42, as amended, 1) adding a condition to
  state, “The easement holder / applicant must maintain the landscaping not to project
  more than seven feet as measured horizontally from the front property line fence.”;
  and 2) determining the project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality
  Act and approving Coastal Development Permit Amendment No. 20-017 to amend
  Coastal Development Permit No. 1 3-040 for the installation of landscaping in the
  City’s public right-of-way to visually screen the recently approved water tank at
  5723 Busch Drive
